questiontext.text:
Secondary-source passage: seventh-century Arabian context

Arabian communities were not isolated. Merchants and travelers moved through routes linking the peninsula to Byzantine, Sasanian, African, and Indian Ocean regions. Mecca combined commercial activity with religious importance. Tribal loyalties remained powerful, but Muhammad’s teachings called believers to worship one God and join a moral community whose obligations included prayer and charity.

Course-authored secondary synthesis based on the Unit 2 crosswalk; this is not a quotation or primary source.
